Introduction

This notebook checks the harmonized, aggregated OsteoCAR reference created by scripts/create-reference.R. The reference combines the primary and metastasis OsteoCAR references into one reference for SingleR with a single level of annotation:

  • Tumor and Mesenchymal labels come from Ann_Level1
  • All other (normal) cell type labels come from Ann_Level2

Labels are harmonized across the two references, so e.g. T cells from both the primary and metastasis references are labeled T_cells.

Here we check that the resulting reference looks as expected:

  1. The object has the expected structure, labels, and values
  2. Known marker genes are most highly expressed in their expected cell types

Setup

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
})

Paths

# find the module root, which contains the renv.lock file
module_base <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_renv_project)
ref_dir <- file.path(module_base, "references")

ref_type <- "patient"
ref_file <- file.path(ref_dir, glue::glue("{ref_type}_harmonized_aggr_ref.rds"))

stopifnot("Reference file does not exist" = file.exists(ref_file))

Read the reference

ref <- readr::read_rds(ref_file)
ref

Structure checks

Labels

Each label should appear once, with no primary_/metastasis_ prefixes and no NA values. The number of pseudobulk samples per label is shown:

table(ref$label, useNA = "ifany")

  Alv_Macrophages           B_cells                DC Endothelial_cells 
               27                69                89               205 
 Epithelial_cells              Mast       Mesenchymal         Monocytes 
              107                42               276                76 
         NK_cells           T_cells              TAMs             Tumor 
               80               192               420               594

Expression values

The logcounts should have no missing values, should not be negative, and no pseudobulk sample should be all zeros.

mat <- assay(ref, "logcounts")

data.frame(
  check = c("Any NA values", "Minimum value", "Maximum value", "Any all-zero columns"),
  result = c(
    anyNA(mat),
    round(min(mat), 3),
    round(max(mat), 3),
    any(colSums(mat) == 0)
  )
)

Average expression per cell type

To compare cell types, we average the pseudobulk samples within each label. This gives a matrix with one row per gene and one column per cell type.

label_avg <- sapply(
  split(seq_len(ncol(mat)), ref$label),
  \(cols) rowMeans(mat[, cols, drop = FALSE])
)

dim(label_avg)
[1] 21332    12

Top expressed genes per cell type

The ten most highly expressed genes in each cell type. Housekeeping genes (e.g., ribosomal genes and MALAT1) are expected to be near the top for all cell types.

Marker gene heatmap

We define four known markers for each cell type in the reference.

marker_list <- list(
  T_cells = c("CD3E", "CD3D", "CD2", "TRAC"),
  NK_cells = c("NKG7", "GNLY", "KLRD1", "KLRF1"),
  B_cells = c("MS4A1", "CD79A", "CD79B", "CD19"),
  Mast = c("TPSAB1", "CPA3", "KIT", "MS4A2"),
  DC = c("CD1C", "FCER1A", "CLEC10A", "CLEC9A"),
  Monocytes = c("CD14", "LYZ", "FCN1", "S100A8"),
  TAMs = c("C1QA", "C1QB", "CD163", "APOE"),
  Alv_Macrophages = c("MARCO", "FABP4", "PPARG", "MSR1"),
  Endothelial_cells = c("PECAM1", "VWF", "CDH5", "KDR"),
  Epithelial_cells = c("EPCAM", "KRT8", "KRT18", "KRT19"),
  Mesenchymal = c("DCN", "LUM", "PDGFRB", "ACTA2"),
  Tumor = c("RUNX2", "SP7", "ALPL", "IBSP")
)

# check that every cell type in the marker list is a label in the reference
stopifnot(
  "Marker list names do not match reference labels" =
    all(names(marker_list) %in% colnames(label_avg))
)

Some markers may not be present in the reference, either because they were not in the original OsteoCAR references or because they were not shared between the primary and metastasis references. These markers are missing and will be left out of the heatmap:

marker_df <- data.frame(
  gene = unlist(marker_list, use.names = FALSE),
  cell_type = rep(names(marker_list), lengths(marker_list))
)

setdiff(marker_df$gene, rownames(label_avg))
[1] "MS4A1"  "CD19"   "MS4A2"  "CLEC9A"
MS4A1
CD19
MS4A2
CLEC9A
marker_df <- marker_df[marker_df$gene %in% rownames(label_avg), ]

Expression is scaled across cell types for each gene.

plot_mat <- label_avg[marker_df$gene, names(marker_list)]

pheatmap::pheatmap(
  plot_mat,
  scale = "row",
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  annotation_row = data.frame(
    cell_type = marker_df$cell_type,
    row.names = marker_df$gene
  ),
  gaps_row = cumsum(table(factor(marker_df$cell_type, levels = names(marker_list)))),
  angle_col = 45
)

Conclusions

  • Marker genes for every cell type are most highly expressed in their expected label, so the aggregated reference profiles are consistent with known biology.
  • Some markers are absent from the reference and were not plotted: MS4A1 and CD19 (B cells), MS4A2 (Mast), and CLEC9A (DC). B cells are therefore represented by only two markers (CD79A, CD79B), though both are specific.
  • Expected overlaps between related cell types are visible:
    • Tumor and Mesenchymal share some signal: Mesenchymal cells express osteoblastic markers (RUNX2, IBSP), and Tumor cells express Mesenchymal markers (DCN, LUM, PDGFRB). This is consistent with the mesenchymal origin of osteosarcoma.
    • Myeloid cell types (Monocytes, DC, TAMs, Alv_Macrophages) share markers such as CD14, LYZ, and C1QA/C1QB. This is expected because they come from a common myeloid lineage, and monocytes can differentiate into macrophages and DCs. As a result, misassignments among these cell types are more likely than between distant lineages.
    • T cells and NK cells share some signal (NKG7 in T cells), as expected for cytotoxic lymphocytes.
    • FCER1A is expressed in both DC and Mast cells, which is known biology.
